newsitem.title: MALDIVES: Indian leader sees fast progress in Pakistan talks.
newsitem.headline: Indian leader sees fast progress in Pakistan talks.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said a meeting later on Monday with his Pakistani counterpart Nawaz Sharif would help the two nations quickly establish neighbourly relations.

Gujral told a summit meeting of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) that he was very encouraged by Sharif's public statements and that progress in bilateral peace talks had been "wholesome".
Gujral and Sharif were set to meet later on Monday at an island resort in the Indian Ocean nation of the Maldives to continue bilateral negotiations which began in March.
"The progress has been wholesome," Gujral said, referring to the two rounds of talks in March and April.
"By grace of God our meeting this afternoon will add another milestone in this shared journey to quickly reach the destination of cooperation and good neighbourliness," the Indian leader said.
"I hope we will make a small contribution in opening a new era of bilateral cooperation and also strengthen SAARC."

Monday's summit would be the first face-to-face meeting between the leaders of the two South Asian neighbours since April 1993, when Sharif and then Indian prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao met on the sidelines of a SAARC conference.
It follows talks between lower-level officials in March and April this year.
"We are determined to continue with this progress so that all outstanding issues can be comprehensively addressed," Sharif said in a speech prepared for delivery at the SAARC inaugural ceremony.
Sharif took office in February after general elections, while Gujral was named prime minister on April 19 following a three-week political crisis in India.
They exchanged letters shortly after Gujral took power, expressing a common desire to press ahead with the peace talks that followed three years of recrimination over the divided region of Kashmir.
Gujral and Sharif are joining leaders from Bangladesh, Bhutan, the Maldives, Nepal and Sri Lanka at the opening of the three-day SAARC summit on Monday.
The two leaders were expected to hold a joint news conference at about 3:30 p.m. (1000 GMT).
